# The tab drag proxy renders at the standalone density, so an inline header's label sits off-centre

## Context

Reported by @tobiu 2026-09-01 against the Workstation: dragging a tab shows a proxy whose label is no longer centred. He then supplied the lead that resolved it — *"maybe related to `ui: 'inline'` => could be broken after we added it."* He is right, and the mechanism is below.

*Separated from inference:* the **observation** is an off-centre label in the drag proxy. The **mechanism** below is confirmed in source but **not yet measured on a live proxy** — driving a real drag needs the cue executor, and no measurement of the running proxy's computed box has been taken. Treat the density numbers as read from the theme, not sampled from a gesture.

## The Problem

`ui: 'inline'` is delivered as a set of CSS custom properties scoped to a **direct-child** selector that requires a `.neo-tab-container-inline` ancestor:

```scss
// resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/tab/Container.scss:18
&.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar,
.neo-tab-container-inline  > .neo-tab-header-toolbar {
    --tab-button-border-radius : 0;
    --tab-button-gap           : 0;
    --tab-button-height        : var(--sem-height-large);
    --tab-button-height-pressed: var(--sem-height-large);
    --tab-button-padding       : 4px var(--sem-spacing-small) 3px;
}
```

The drag proxy is built as a **detached toolbar rooted at `document.body`**, and it inherits the owning toolbar's own class list:

```javascript
// src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:446 — the seam every tab drag actually goes through
getDragProxyConfig() {
    return {...this.dragProxyConfig, cls: [...this.owner.cls]}
}
```

**Correction, 2026-09-01 — an earlier revision of this ticket said the proxy "clones two classes and nothing else" and pointed at the static `dragProxyConfig` literal in `SortZone.mjs:23`. That was wrong, and a peer implementing against it would have edited a dead field.** `cls` comes after the spread, so the static literal's `cls` is overwritten by `this.owner.cls`; the proxy actually carries the source toolbar's full class list, plus the theme/language classes `dashboard.dock.interaction.TabSortZone#getDragProxyConfig` resolves by ancestor walk, plus `neo-dragproxy`.

**The defect is unchanged, and the correction makes it sharper:** `neo-tab-container-inline` lives on the tab.**Container**, never on the toolbar, so it is not in `owner.cls` and cannot be. And because the variant is expressed as a *descendant* rule — `.neo-tab-container-inline > .neo-tab-header-toolbar` — no class on the proxy alone can satisfy it: the proxy is body-rooted and has no such ancestor. The tokens never resolve and the button falls back to the theme's `ui: null` contract:

| | `--tab-button-height` | `--tab-button-padding` |
|---|---|---|
| source header (`ui: 'inline'`) | **32px** | `4px 12px 3px` |
| drag proxy (falls back to `null`) | **48px** | `7px 16px 6px` |

A 16px height difference and 4px more horizontal padding, applied to a button whose geometry came from a 32px header — the label is vertically off-centre and horizontally shifted for the whole gesture.

**Why it reads as a regression.** Before the `ui` variants existed there was exactly one header density, so the proxy's fallback happened to match its source. Introducing `inline` (`#17950` / `#17956`) made the fallback wrong without touching the proxy; nothing in that change had a reason to look at `SortZone`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:446` — `getDragProxyConfig()` is the live seam: it returns the owning toolbar's `cls`, overwriting whatever `cls` the static `dragProxyConfig` declares. `src/draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` does **not** override it; `dashboard.dock.interaction.TabSortZone` does, and appends theme/language by walking ancestors — which is the precedent for propagating a variant the same way. Neither consults the owning container's `ui`, so no per-consumer variant reaches the proxy.
- `resources/scss/theme-{light,dark,neo-light,neo-dark}/tab/Container.scss` — all four themes scope the variant tokens the same way: on the **container**, applied to its direct-child toolbar. The variant is a container-level contract, and the proxy is not a container's child.
- `src/component/Base.mjs:894` (`afterSetUi`) emits `neo-<ntype>-<ui>` on the **container**, which is exactly the ancestor the proxy lacks.
- `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs:96` — `dragProxyConfig_` is the generic seam; any fix here should stay in the tab-specific SortZone unless the same gap is shown for other consumers.

**Ruled out during triage, recorded so it is not re-walked:** `#17963` (`fa20136f29`) was the obvious suspect on timing, since it rewrote `src/tab/header/Toolbar.scss` — the sheet whose class the proxy clones. It is **not** the cause: that commit only *added* a nested `&.neo-toolbar > .neo-toolbar-action.neo-button` block, and the proxy carries a tab **button**, not an action.

## The Fix

`src/draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` plus the four theme sheets, or a single self-scoped selector — one of:

1. **Propagate the owner's variant onto the proxy** and let the variant selector match the toolbar itself: extend each theme's rule to `.neo-tab-header-toolbar.neo-tab-container-inline` (self-scoped, alongside the existing descendant form), and have the SortZone add the owning container's `ui`-derived class to `dragProxyConfig.cls` at drag start. Keeps one token source.
2. **Copy the resolved token values** onto the proxy at drag start. Rejected as a default because it snapshots values rather than participating in the cascade — a theme switch mid-drag would strand them — but it is the smaller change if 1 proves awkward.

Adding `neo-tab-container-inline` to the proxy's `cls` **alone does nothing**: the existing selector requires the class on the parent, and the proxy *is* the toolbar. That is the trap this ticket exists to document.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `draggable.tab.header.toolbar.SortZone#getDragProxyConfig()` (new override) | this ticket | the proxy carries the owning container's `ui`-derived class so variant tokens resolve on it | none — a proxy at the wrong density is the defect | method JSDoc names why the class is propagated rather than hardcoded, and that `cls` here overwrites the static literal | computed `--tab-button-height` / `--tab-button-padding` on the live proxy equal the source header's |
| the four `tab/Container.scss` variant blocks | `#17950` / `#17956` | gain a self-scoped form so a detached toolbar can match | descendant form unchanged for the in-container case | in-sheet comment naming the detached-proxy case | a proxy measured at 32px under `inline`, 48px under `null` |

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tab dragged out of an `ui: 'inline'` header produces a proxy whose `--tab-button-height` and `--tab-button-padding` equal the source header's — asserted on the **live proxy during a gesture**, not on a static fixture.
- [ ] The same arm reds before the fix. A proxy-geometry assertion that passes at both ends proves nothing, and there is currently **no** proxy-geometry coverage anywhere in `test/playwright/` to inherit.
- [ ] The `ui: null` / `standalone` cases are unchanged — the proxy still matches *its* source header, so the fix is "the proxy inherits its owner's variant", not "the proxy is always inline".
- [ ] The gesture is driven through the app's own cue executor (`Workspace#executeCue`) or an equivalently trusted pointer path. The browser tool's synthetic click cannot arm a drag sensor, so a proxy that never exists would read as a green assertion.
- [ ] The JSDoc on the new `getDragProxyConfig()` override states why the class is propagated, and that `cls` there overwrites the static `dragProxyConfig` literal, so the next variant added does not silently repeat this.

## Out of Scope

- **The other drag-proxy consumers.** `DragZone#dragProxyConfig` is generic; whether container/grid/dashboard proxies have the same variant gap is a separate census, not assumed here.
- **`#17889`'s Pointer Events migration.** Adjacent surface, unrelated mechanism.
- **The label-overlap defect** witnessed by `WorkstationTabDragLabelOverlapNL` — two different heading strings interleaving on one baseline is a different failure, and that spec is red for its own reasons.
- Any change to what `ui: 'inline'` means. This ticket makes the proxy honour the existing contract; it does not renegotiate it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding the variant class to the proxy and stopping there.** The selector needs it on the parent; the proxy is the toolbar. This looks like a one-line fix and is a no-op.
- **Blaming `#17963` on timing.** It rewrote the very sheet the proxy clones and landed the day the symptom appeared, which is exactly the shape of a false positive. Its added rule is action-scoped and the proxy carries a tab button.
- **Asserting proxy geometry from a static fixture.** The proxy only exists mid-gesture; a spec that builds a lookalike measures its own construction.
